extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining entitlement to and calculating patent term adjustment (PTA) under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and implementing regulations 37 CFR 1.702-1.705, including periods of Office delay, exclusions, reductions for applicant delay, IDS safe harbors, and what constitutes condition for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and effective dates (37 CFR 1.702(f) and related provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.702-1.705 apply only to original applications (except design) filed on or after May 29, 2000, and patents issued on such applications; several versions of the rules exist with different effective dates and must be applied carefully to the particular application or patent under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel must carefully consider effective date provisions (e.g., differences for patents granted on or after Jan 14, 2013, notices of allowance on or after Sept 17, 2012, etc.) to determine which version applies to a given application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to PTA for Office failure to perform certain acts (37 CFR 1.702(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is entitled to patent term adjustment if the Office fails to perform certain acts of examination within specified time frames (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general ground is implemented by specific period measurements set forth in 37 CFR 1.703(a)(1)-(6). For patents granted on or after Jan 14, 2013, 1.703(a)(1) provides the 14-month measurement for mailing a notification under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for 14-month measurement (37 CFR 1.703(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of days, if any, beginning the day after the date that is fourteen months after the date the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (or date national stage commenced) and ending on the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications filed on/after May 29, 2000 and patents granted prior to Jan 14, 2013, the 14-month measurement may be based on the date the application fulfilled 35 U.S.C. 371 rather than national stage commencement. See applicable versions of 1.703.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-month periods following specific applicant filings (37 CFR 1.703(a)(2)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each four-month period begins the day after the date that is four months after specified applicant filings and ends on mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first: (2) reply under § 1.111; (3) reply in compliance with § 1.113(c); (4) appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are separate subperiods to be added to the PTA under 1.702(a) to the extent they exist and do not overlap with other PTO delay periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-month period after final decision with at least one allowable claim (37 CFR 1.703(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of days, if any, beginning the day after the date that is four months after the date of a final decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board or by a Federal court in an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 where at least one allowable claim remains, and ending on the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied only when at least one allowable claim remains in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-month period after issue fee payment and satisfaction of requirements (37 CFR 1.703(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of days, if any, beginning the day after the date that is four months after the date the issue fee was paid and all outstanding requirements were satisfied and ending on the date a patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts delay after applicant took final issuance steps until patent issuance, subject to overlap rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year delay entitlement (37 CFR 1.702(b) / 1.703(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is entitled to patent term adjustment if, subject to limitations, the Office fails to issue a patent within three years of the actual filing date of the application (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(B)). The period begins the day after three years from filing (or national stage commencement) and ends on the date a patent was issued, excluding specified applicant and other excluded periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-year period is reduced by specified periods such as the time consumed by RCEs, interference/derivation, secrecy, and PTAB jurisdiction (see 1.703(b)(1)-(4)). Effective Jan 9, 2015, 1.703(b)(1) defines time consumed by RCEs as from filing date of RCE until mailing of notice of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for time consumed by RCEs (37 CFR 1.703(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude from the three-year period the number of days, if any, beginning on the date any request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) was filed and ending on the date of mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE time is not counted as PTO delay for the three-year calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions for interference/derivation proceedings (37 CFR 1.703(b)(2) & 1.703(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude periods when an interference or derivation proceeding was instituted involving the application or when prosecution was suspended because of interference/derivation proceedings not involving the application; for §1.702(c) entitlement, sum the days from institution to termination and suspension periods to the extent they don't overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the AIA, derivation proceedings replaced interferences for certain applications; include derivation proceedings in the guarantees of adjustment for Office delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions for secrecy orders (37 CFR 1.703(b)(3) & 1.703(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude days the application was maintained in a sealed condition under 35 U.S.C. 181, and related subsections concerning examiner's answers mailed under secrecy order, notification of potential interference, and notification under § 5.3(c) ending on mailing of notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy-related periods are excluded from the three-year clock and counted in the secrecy-delay entitlement when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB jurisdiction exclusion and appellate-review entitlement (37 CFR 1.703(b)(4) & 1.703(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude time during which jurisdiction passed to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under § 41.35(a) until PTAB jurisdiction ended under § 41.35(b) (or last federal decision), for three-year exclusion; separately, § 1.702(e)/1.703(e) entitles a patent to adjustment for days from passage of jurisdiction to PTAB under § 41.45(a) until a final decision in favor of the applicant by PTAB or a Federal court appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments for appellate review were revised to reflect AIA changes; 1.703(e) applies to appellate review delays that result in final decision in favor of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap limitation and calculation formula (37 CFR 1.703(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent periods of delay attributable to grounds specified in § 1.702 overlap, the period of adjustment shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed. The patent term is adjusted for the sum of periods under paragraphs (a) through (e) to the extent not overlapping, less the sum of periods calculated under § 1.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on any certificate of mailing or transmission under § 1.8 shall not be taken into account in this calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction for applicant failure to engage reasonable efforts (37 CFR 1.704(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment shall be reduced by a period equal to the period during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General reduction principle; detailed circumstances constituting failure are provided in 1.704(b)-(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month cumulative reply rule (37 CFR 1.704(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is deemed to have failed to engage in reasonable efforts for the cumulative total of any periods in excess of three months taken to reply to any Office notice or action that makes a rejection, objection, argument, or other request, measuring the three-month period from the date the notice or action was mailed or given to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction equals days beginning the day after three months from mailing/transmission of the Office communication until the reply was filed. The shorter statutory reply period in the Office action does not affect this three-month measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action at applicant's request (37 CFR 1.704(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If action is suspended under § 1.103 at the applicant's request, the period of adjustment is reduced by the number of days beginning on the date a request for suspension was filed and ending on the date the suspension terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-requested suspensions count as applicant delay for reduction purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of issuance of patent (37 CFR 1.704(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant requests deferral of issuance under § 1.314, reduce adjustment by days from the date the deferral request was filed until the earlier of termination of deferral request or the patent issuance date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral periods requested by applicant shorten PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment or late payment of issue fee (37 CFR 1.704(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application was abandoned or the issue fee was paid late, reduce adjustment by days beginning on the date of abandonment or the day after the issue fee due date and ending on the date a grantable petition to revive or accept late payment was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late actions by the applicant that interrupt prosecution are charged against PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to petition to withdraw abandonment holding within two months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition to withdraw holding of abandonment or to revive the application is not filed within two months from mailing of the notice of abandonment, reduce adjustment by days beginning the day after two months from mailing of the abandonment notice until the petition was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's failure to timely petition to revive reduces PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of provisional to nonprovisional (37 CFR 1.704(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting a provisional under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) to a nonprovisional under 111(a) pursuant to 111(b)(5), reduce adjustment by days beginning on the provisional's filing date and ending on the date a request in compliance with § 1.53(c)(3) to convert was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion-related time prior to conversion request can be charged as applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment or other paper less than one month before Office action causing supplemental action (37 CFR 1.704(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper less than one month before mailing of an Office action or notice of allowance that requires mailing of a supplemental Office action or notice will reduce adjustment by days beginning the day after the date that is eight months from filing (or national stage commencement) and ending on the date the preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule prevents applicants from filing last-minute materials that trigger additional PTO work from earning PTA for the intervening period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply having an omission (37 CFR 1.704(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a reply having an omission under § 1.135(c), reduce adjustment by days beginning the day after the date the reply with omission was filed and ending on the date the reply or other paper correcting the omission was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitted items that require correction create applicant-charged delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply or other paper after a reply (unrequested) (37 CFR 1.704(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a supplemental reply or other paper (other than requested by examiner) after a reply reduces adjustment by days beginning the day after the date the initial reply was filed and ending on the date the supplemental reply or other paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsolicited additional submissions after a reply are treated as applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment after PTAB or court decision less than one month before action requiring supplemental mailing (37 CFR 1.704(c)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment or other paper after a PTAB or Federal court decision, other than certain PTAB new-ground decisions, less than one month before mailing of an Office action or a notice of allowance that requires supplemental mailing reduces adjustment by days beginning the day after the decision and ending on the date the amendment or paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late amendments following appellate decisions that trigger more PTO work reduce PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment under § 1.312 or other paper after notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment under § 1.312 or other paper (except examiner-requested or an RCE under § 1.114) after a notice of allowance has been given or mailed reduces adjustment by days beginning the day after mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 and ending on the date the amendment or other paper was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-allowance amendments/communications requested by applicant cut PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file appeal brief within three months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three months from the date a notice of appeal was filed under 35 U.S.C. 134 reduces adjustment by days beginning the day after the date three months from filing the notice of appeal and ending on the date an appeal brief or RCE in compliance with § 1.114 was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely appeal briefs are applicant delay subject to reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.704(c)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) after any notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 has been mailed reduces adjustment by days beginning the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-allowance RCEs are charged to applicant and reduce PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide application in condition for examination within eight months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is not in condition for examination within eight months from filing (or national stage commencement), reduce adjustment by days beginning the day after the date that is eight months from filing and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination as defined in paragraph (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition-for-examination elements are defined in 1.704(f); failure to be ready in time reduces PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of further prosecution via continuing application (37 CFR 1.704(c)(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: For further prosecution via a continuing application, the period of adjustment shall not include any period that is prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay attributable to earlier-filed applications does not count toward PTA for the later application.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS-only safe harbor and required PTA statement (37 CFR 1.704(d)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an IDS in compliance with §§ 1.97 and 1.98 (or an RCE containing only an IDS) will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under certain 1.704 paragraphs if accompanied by a statement that each IDS item was first cited in a communication from a counterpart foreign/international office or was issued by a patent office and not received more than 30 days prior to filing the IDS. The statement must be on PTO/SB/133 using document code PTA.IDS and may not be altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the form is not used or is altered, the paper or RCE will be treated as not accompanied by the required statement and may be considered applicant delay. Presentation of the form constitutes a certification under § 11.18(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement request under § 1.705(c) not considered failure (37 CFR 1.704(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced patent term adjustment will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under paragraph (c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a §1.705(c) reinstatement request does not itself create additional applicant-delay reductions under the post-allowance submission rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for examination defined (37 CFR 1.704(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes a specification with at least one claim and an abstract (§ 1.72(b)), papers in compliance with § 1.52, drawings if any (§ 1.84), any required English translations, Sequence Listing/Sequence Listing XML (if applicable), an inventor’s oath/declaration or ADS with § 1.63(b) info, basic filing/search/examination fees, any certified copy required by § 1.57(a), and any application size fee required under § 1.16(s). International applications must have entered the national stage and include analogous items and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is used for applying the eight-month condition-for-examination rule and other timing rules; missing elements mean the application is not ready and applicant delay may be charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by PTAB treated as decision in review for PTA purposes (37 CFR 1.702(e) / MPEP guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A remand by a panel of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board is considered a decision by the Board as that phrase is used in 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)(iii) and a decision in the review reversing an adverse determination of patentability for PTA if the remand is the last action by the Board prior to mailing of a notice of allowance, except when a subsequent RCE is filed that was not first preceded by an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply when remands are followed by RCEs or other actions; see MPEP for when remands count as appellate-review delay favorable to applicant.
